breakfast.name: Panipopo (Coconut Bread Rolls)
ingredients: Dough: flour, yeast, sugar, milk, butter
Coconut cream sauce: coconut cream, sugar
instructions: Make sweet dough, rise
Shape into rolls
Pour coconut cream sauce over
Bake at 175°C 25 min until golden
breakfast.description: Sweet bread rolls baked in coconut cream — Samoa's favorite.

breakfast.name: Boiled Taro with Coconut Cream
instructions: Boil taro until tender
Drizzle with coconut cream and salt

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Thierry Caro assumed (based on copyright claims).

breakfast.name: Pani Popo (Coconut Buns)
ingredients: Bread dough (flour, yeast, sugar, milk, butter)
instructions: Pani popo are Samoan coconut cream buns -- the most beloved Samoan sweet
The dough is a soft, enriched bread dough
The buns are placed in a baking pan with coconut cream poured over
As they bake, the coconut cream caramelizes and the buns absorb it
The result: soft buns with a sticky, sweet coconut glaze on top
Pani popo is served at Samoan celebrations and Sunday faalavelave
breakfast.description: Samoan coconut cream buns -- enriched bread dough buns baked in coconut cream that caramelizes and is absorbed by the buns, creating a sticky sweet glaze. The most beloved Samoan sweet. Served at celebrations and the Sunday faalavelave (community gatherings).

breakfast.name: Koko Samoa (Samoan Cocoa Tea)
ingredients: Koko Samoa (raw Samoan cacao -- ground into a paste or as nibs)
instructions: Koko Samoa is the traditional Samoan cacao drink
Samoan cacao: grown in the Samoan islands -- a heritage crop
The cacao is processed minimally -- ground into a rough paste or nibs
Dissolved in hot water, with coconut cream added
Much more complex and earthy than commercial hot chocolate
The cacao trees have been grown in Samoa for generations
breakfast.description: Samoan traditional cacao drink -- raw Samoan cacao (ground rough or as nibs) dissolved in hot water with coconut cream added. Much more complex and earthy than hot chocolate. Samoan cacao is a heritage crop grown on the islands for generations.

lunch.name: Oka (Raw Fish Salad)
instructions: Marinate fish in lime 15 min
Drain, add coconut cream
Toss with vegetables
Serve cold
lunch.description: Samoan raw fish in lime and coconut cream.

lunch.name: Palusami (Taro Leaves in Coconut)
instructions: Layer taro leaves, fill with coconut cream and onion
Wrap in foil or banana leaves
Bake 2 hours
lunch.description: Taro leaves slow-cooked in rich coconut cream.

lunch.name: Sapasui (Samoan Chop Suey)
instructions: Sapasui is the Samoan version of chap chye -- Chinese influence on Samoan food
Samoan chop suey -- a stir-fry of glass noodles with meat and vegetables
The Chinese migrant community in Samoa (from the early 1900s) brought noodle dishes
The sapasui became completely Samoan over the decades
Glass noodles absorb the flavors of the soy sauce and meat
Served at every Samoan faalavelave -- no community feast without sapasui
lunch.description: Samoan glass noodle stir-fry -- glass noodles (cellophane) with chicken or beef, cabbage, and aromatics in soy sauce. Chinese-Samoan heritage: brought by Chinese migrants in the early 1900s and completely Samoananized. No community feast (faalavelave) is complete without sapasui.

imageCredit.author: Eli Hodapp from Naperville, United States

lunch.name: Taro and Corned Beef
instructions: Taro and canned corned beef is the contemporary Samoan everyday combination
Taro: the ancient staple of Polynesia -- the most important traditional food
Canned corned beef arrived with Western contact and became beloved
The combination of ancient taro and canned corned beef tells the story of modern Samoa
Simply cooked: taro boiled, corned beef sauteed with onion
Often coconut cream added to the taro for richness
lunch.description: Samoan everyday combination -- boiled taro (the ancient Polynesian staple) with canned corned beef (arrived with Western contact) sauteed with onion. The combination of ancient starch and modern canned meat tells the story of contemporary Samoa. Coconut cream often added to the taro.

lunch.name: Oka (Samoan Raw Fish)
ingredients: Fresh fish (mahi-mahi, tuna, or snapper -- must be very fresh)
Lime juice (enough to marinate the fish)
instructions: Oka is the Samoan raw fish -- the Polynesian ceviche
The fresh fish is cut into chunks and marinated in lime juice
The lime juice cooks the fish through acid denaturation
After 20-30 minutes, the fish is opaque and firm
Coconut cream is then added -- the richness is the Samoan element
Served cold with onion, cucumber, and tomato
lunch.description: Samoan raw fish ceviche-style -- fresh fish cut into chunks and acid-cooked in lime juice (20-30 minutes until opaque), then enriched with coconut cream, tossed with onion, cucumber, and tomato. The coconut cream is the Samoan distinction from other Pacific raw fish dishes.

dinner.name: Umu (Earth Oven Feast)
instructions: Heat stones in fire
Wrap food in banana leaves
Layer over hot stones in pit
Cover with earth and leaves
Cook 3 hours
Uncover and serve communally
dinner.description: Traditional earth oven feast — the heart of Samoan Sunday.

dinner.name: Sapasui (Chop Suey)
instructions: Brown beef, add vegetables
Add soy sauce
Cook noodles, add to beef
Toss together
dinner.description: Samoan-Chinese chop suey with glass noodles.

imageCredit.author: Eli Hodapp from Naperville, United States

dinner.name: Palusami (Taro Leaves in Coconut Cream)
instructions: Palusami is the Samoan dish of taro leaves cooked in coconut cream
Young taro leaves are more tender and less astringent
The leaves are wrapped around the coconut cream filling
Or: the leaves are placed in a coconut shell or foil packet with cream
Cooked in the umu (earth oven) traditionally -- in the oven today
The coconut cream absorbs into the leaves -- they become silky and rich
Palusami is the Samoan celebration dish -- served at weddings and faalavelave
dinner.description: Samoan taro leaves in coconut cream -- young taro leaves wrapped around coconut cream and onion, cooked in the umu (earth oven) or conventional oven until the leaves are silky and the cream is absorbed. The Samoan celebration dish for weddings and faalavelave.

dinner.name: Lu Sipi (Lamb Flaps Palusami)
instructions: Lu sipi is the Samoan lamb version of palusami
Lamb flaps (fatty breast pieces) are the Polynesian Pacific cut
Wrapped in taro leaves with coconut cream
The fat from the lamb renders into the coconut cream
The combination of lamb fat and coconut cream: intensely rich
Lamb was introduced to the Pacific -- New Zealand lamb is now a Samoan staple
dinner.description: Samoan lamb flaps in taro leaves -- fatty lamb breast pieces (New Zealand lamb, a Pacific staple) wrapped in taro leaves with coconut cream, slow-cooked until the fat renders into the cream. The richness of lamb fat and coconut cream is intense. The meat version of palusami.

dinner.name: Sapolo (Samoan Chili)
instructions: Sapolo is the Samoan adaptation of American chili -- Western contact food
American influence on Samoa: via the US Navy, canned goods, and American Samoa
American Samoa (US territory) and independent Samoa share food traditions
Canned goods (kidney beans, tomatoes) became staples
Sapolo is simple, quick, and filling
dinner.description: Samoan chili -- American influence via US Navy and American Samoa (US territory). Ground beef with canned tomatoes, kidney beans, and chili powder. Simple and filling. Canned goods became Samoan pantry staples through Western contact.

snacks.name: Fa'ausi (Coconut Caramel)
instructions: Cook coconut cream with sugar until thick and caramel-like
Serve over bread or taro

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Thierry Caro assumed (based on copyright claims).

snacks.name: Fa'apapa (Coconut Biscuits)
instructions: Fa'apapa are Samoan coconut cream biscuits -- simple and loved
The coconut cream replaces water or milk in the dough
Baked until golden -- they become firm and slightly crispy
Eaten as a snack with tea
snacks.description: Samoan coconut cream biscuits -- flour-based dough made with coconut cream instead of water, baked until golden and firm. Simple and deeply coconutty. Eaten with tea.

snacks.name: Panipopo (Mini Coconut Buns)
ingredients: Same as pani popo but smaller
instructions: The mini version of pani popo -- single-serving coconut buns
The same concept: buns baked in coconut cream
Smaller and sold at Samoan markets and tuck shops
snacks.description: Mini Samoan coconut cream buns -- smaller version of pani popo, baked in sweetened coconut cream. Sold at Samoan markets and tuck shops.

snacks.name: Keke (Fried Scones)
instructions: Keke are Samoan fried scones -- quick, filling, and popular
The dough is mixed and dropped into hot oil
Fried until golden and puffed
Eaten plain or with butter and jam
The everyday Samoan snack
snacks.description: Samoan fried scones -- simple flour-coconut cream dough dropped into hot oil and fried until golden and puffed. Eaten plain or with butter and jam. The everyday Samoan quick snack.

desserts.name: Koko Alaisa (Cocoa Rice)
instructions: Cook rice
Stir in cocoa, sugar, coconut cream
Serve warm
desserts.description: Sweet cocoa rice in coconut cream.

desserts.name: Tapioca Pudding
instructions: Tapioca comes from cassava -- a Pacific staple
Cooked in coconut milk -- the Samoan way
The tapioca pearls become translucent and chewy
Sweetened and served with tropical fruit
desserts.description: Samoan tapioca in coconut milk -- tapioca pearls cooked in coconut milk until translucent and chewy, sweetened with sugar and vanilla, served with mango or passion fruit. Cassava-derived tapioca meets Pacific coconut milk.

desserts.name: Banana Poke
instructions: Banana poke is a Polynesian baked banana dessert
Poke in Polynesian means to pound or press -- a poke is a mashed, baked pudding
The ripe bananas are mashed and combined with coconut cream
Baked until set -- the coconut cream firms up
desserts.description: Polynesian baked banana pudding -- very ripe bananas mashed and combined with coconut cream and cinnamon, baked until set. Poke in Polynesian means a mashed, baked pudding. Simple and tropical.

drinks.name: Koko Samoa (Samoan Cocoa)
instructions: Boil water, add ground cocoa
Simmer 10 min
Add sugar and coconut cream

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open, drink fresh

drinks.name: Fresh Coconut Water
instructions: Young coconut water is the original Samoan drink
The green coconuts are cut with a machete -- the water pours out
The young coconut water is naturally sweet and refreshing
In hot Pacific weather, coconut water is the natural electrolyte drink
After drinking the water, the young coconut flesh (jelly) is scooped out
drinks.description: Fresh young coconut water -- green coconut cut open with a machete for the naturally sweet, electrolyte-rich water inside. In hot Pacific weather the natural refreshment. After drinking, the soft jelly flesh is scooped out and eaten.
